description: Je suis étudiant en Licence de Robotique et passionné par les technologies innovantes ayant un impact concret sur la société. Mes centres d’intérêt sont la robotique, l’intelligence artificielle, les systèmes embarqués, l’impression 3D, la programmation et les technologies spatiales. Je souhaite créer une équipe motivée pour relever ensemble le défi du NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
**Badr Health** is a local AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed for long-duration space missions. Our solution combines real-time physiological data, rule-based safety alerts, and an offline medical AI assistant powered by BioMistral running locally through Ollama.

The system continuously monitors vital signs such as heart rate, blood oxygen level, body temperature, and blood pressure, while identifying abnormal trends and potential health risks. Unlike cloud-dependent solutions, all medical data remain on the local device, ensuring privacy, low latency, and operation even without an internet connection—an essential requirement for deep-space missions.

Badr Health addresses the challenge by providing astronauts and mission crews with an intelligent "second opinion" that complements, rather than replaces, established medical protocols. Threshold-based alerts remain authoritative, while the AI generates structured medical reviews and guided symptom assessments to support informed decision-making.

By combining secure local AI, continuous monitoring, and explainable medical assistance, Badr Health improves crew safety, autonomy, and resilience during future lunar and deep-space exploration missions.
details:
Badr Health is an AI-assisted health monitoring and decision-support platform designed for astronauts during long-duration space missions. The system continuously collects and displays physiological data, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, blood pressure, and other mission-relevant health indicators. These measurements are analyzed through a combination of deterministic medical safety rules and an on-device artificial intelligence assistant.

Our solution uses a hybrid approach. Critical threshold alerts remain independent and rule-based to ensure reliability, while the BioMistral medical language model provides a structured medical review, identifies potential health concerns, and supports guided symptom assessment. Running the AI locally through Ollama allows the system to operate without an internet connection, reducing latency and protecting sensitive medical data.

The project was designed with privacy, reliability, and astronaut autonomy as core principles. Since communication delays increase significantly during lunar and deep-space missions, astronauts cannot always rely on immediate support from Earth. Badr Health offers an intelligent "second opinion" that assists crew members while keeping the final medical decision under established mission protocols.

To develop the project, we used TypeScript, React, Vite, Python, Supabase, Ollama, and the BioMistral open-source medical language model. The backend provides secure local AI analysis, while the frontend offers an intuitive dashboard for monitoring crew health, reviewing alerts, and interacting with the AI assistant. The project also includes simulated astronaut health data to demonstrate anomaly detection and medical reasoning in an offline environment.

Creativity was a major focus of our work. Instead of replacing medical procedures, our system combines explainable AI with transparent rule-based monitoring, ensuring that AI recommendations remain supportive rather than authoritative. We also considered data privacy, offline operation, low computational requirements, future integration with wearable biomedical sensors, and scalability for future lunar habitats and deep-space exploration missions.

Badr Health demonstrates how local artificial intelligence can improve astronaut safety, support autonomous medical monitoring, and strengthen mission resilience while respecting the strict operational constraints of human space exploration.
